The left graph is labeled s_1(t), and within the first half-bit time from 0 to T_B/2 it is a rectangular pulse of height A_0, and within the second half-bit time from T_B/2 to T_B it is 0. The right graph is labeled s_2(t), and within 0 to T_B/2 it is 0, and within the second half-bit time from T_B/2 to T_B it is a rectangular pulse of height A_0. Therefore the two are two non-overlapping half-bit rectangular pulses. Reasoning: The squared Euclidean distance is d_{12}^2 = ∫_0^{T_B}[s_1(t)-s_2(t)]^2 dt. In the first half segment, s_1-s_2=A_0, contributing A_0^2 T_B/2; in the second half segment, s_1-s_2=-A_0, contributing A_0^2 T_B/2. So d_{12}^2=A_0^2 T_B. For binary equiprobable AWGN optimal reception, if the two-sided noise power spectral density is n_0/2, then the bit error rate P_e = 1/2 erfc(sqrt(d_{12}^2/(4 n_0))). Substituting d_{12}^2=A_0^2 T_B gives P_e = 1/2 erfc(sqrt(A_0^2 T_B/(4 n_0))).

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a pulse-position binary signaling scheme with one pulse in either the first or second half of the bit interval. Form a receiver statistic Z = ∫0^{TB/2} r(t)A0 dt - ∫_{TB/2}^{TB} r(t)A0 dt, or equivalently compare correlations with s1 and s2.
